summary:
**TerraTone AI – NASA Earth Information Jukebox**

TerraTone AI is an interactive web application that transforms NASA Earth imagery into sound, making Earth science visualizations more accessible, especially for people who are blind or have low vision. The project allows users to load satellite images from NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS) or upload Earth imagery. It analyzes visual features such as brightness, colour balance, and image patterns, then converts them into musical tones and rhythms. Users can listen to the generated audio, explore different sound-mapping modes, and download the results. By connecting visual information with sound, TerraTone AI offers an alternative way to experience changes and patterns in our planet. This project aims to make NASA Earth observation data more inclusive, interactive, and engaging for everyone.
details:
Project Details – TerraTone AI

TerraTone AI is an interactive web application developed for the NASA Earth Information Jukebox challenge. Its main objective is to convert Earth observation images into sound, providing an alternative way to experience satellite imagery, especially for people who are blind or have low vision.

The application allows users to select satellite imagery through NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS) or upload their own images. It uses image processing techniques to analyze visual features such as brightness and colour balance. These features are mapped into musical pitches and rhythms to generate audio. Users can explore different sonification modes, listen to the generated sounds, and download the audio in WAV format.

Technologies Used: Python, Streamlit, NumPy, Pillow, Matplotlib, Requests, and audio signal synthesis.

Benefits and Impact: TerraTone AI aims to improve accessibility, encourage inclusive learning, and provide a new way to explore patterns in Earth imagery through listening.

Role of AI: AI assistance was used during development for brainstorming, code assistance, debugging, and improving project documentation. The core prototype uses image processing and rule-based sound mapping rather than a trained machine-learning model.

Future Scope: We plan to improve synchronized image-to-sound playback, integrate more NASA Earth datasets, and evaluate the application with blind and low-vision users.
